Hello, I'm so glad you're here today. My name is [Your Name], and I'm a clinician specializing in postpartum mental health. I want to start by acknowledging the incredible journey you've been on, bringing a new life into the world. This can be a truly overwhelming yet joyful time, and I'm here to support you every step of the way.

As part of our conversation today, I'd like to use the EPDS to help us better understand how you're feeling and to identify any potential areas where we can offer additional support. The EPDS is a tool that helps us screen for depressive and anxiety symptoms, which can be common during the postpartum period. It's completely confidential, and everything we discuss today will remain between us.

Please know that you're in a safe and supportive space, and I'm here to listen without judgment. My goal is to provide you with a comfortable and non-intrusive experience, allowing you to share your feelings and thoughts openly. The EPDS consists of 10 questions that will help us get a better sense of your emotional well-being over the past 7 days.

We'll take this one question at a time, and I'll do my best to make this conversation feel as natural and effortless as possible. So, let's get started. Here's my first question: Over the past 7 days, have you been able to laugh and see the funny side of things?

.. (sigh) To be honest, it's been really hard for me to find the humor in things lately. I mean, I used to be a pretty happy person, always laughing and joking around, but since having the baby, it's just been so... overwhelming. I feel like I'm just trying to get through each day, you know? And when I do try to laugh or watch something funny, it just doesn't feel the same. It's like, I'll be watching a comedy or something, and I'll think to myself, "Oh, this should be funny," but it just doesn't make me laugh like it used to. (pausing, looking down) I don't know, maybe I'm just too tired all the time. I feel like I'm just going through the motions, and laughter just isn't coming as easily to me anymore. (looking up, slightly tearful) Does that make sense?
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

(shaking head) No... not really. Like I said, it's just been hard for me to find the humor in things lately. I mean, I might smile or laugh occasionally, but it's not like it used to be. It feels forced, you know? Like, I'll be playing with the baby, and she'll do something cute, and I'll smile, but it's not the same as really laughing and feeling carefree. (sighing) Most of the time, I just feel anxious or worried about something, and it's hard to shake that off. Even when I do try to relax and have fun, my mind starts wandering to all the things I need to do or worry about, and it's just... (trailing off, looking down) hard.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things

(sighing) Honestly, not as much as I used to. I mean, I'll think about doing something I used to enjoy, like going for a walk or reading a book, and I'll think, "Oh, that sounds nice," but when it comes down to it, I just don't feel like doing it. Or, I'll start to do it, and then I'll just feel overwhelmed and anxious, and I'll stop. (pausing) I don't know, it's like I've lost interest in things that used to bring me joy. Even things like spending time with my baby, which I know I should be enjoying, just feel like a chore sometimes. (looking down, voice dropping to a whisper) I feel guilty about that, because I know I should be loving every moment with her, but it's just not how I'm feeling right now. (wiping away a tear) Sorry...
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

(nodding) Yeah... I do that a lot. I mean, if the baby is crying and I'm trying to soothe her, and I feel like I'm not doing it right, I'll just start thinking, "What's wrong with me? Why can't I do this?" Or, if I'm feeling really overwhelmed and I need to ask for help, I'll think, "I'm a bad mom for not being able to handle this on my own." (shaking head) It's like, I know it's not rational, but I just can't help feeling like I'm not doing enough, or that I'm not good enough. (sighing) And it's not just with the baby, it's with everything. If I'm tired and I need a break, I'll think, "You're so lazy, you should be able to handle this." (looking down) It's like, I'm just really hard on myself, and it's exhausting. (pausing, voice cracking) Sometimes I feel like I'm just waiting for someone to tell me that I'm doing everything wrong, and that I'm a terrible mom. (tearfully) Does that sound crazy?
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

(nodding vigorously) Oh, yeah... that's me all the time. I mean, I'll be sitting there, feeding the baby or changing her diaper, and suddenly I'll just start worrying about something. Like, what if she's not gaining enough weight? Or what if I'm not producing enough milk? Or what if... (trailing off) I don't know, it's just always something. And it's not even like it's rational, it's just this constant, nagging feeling of "what if?" (rubbing hands together nervously) And it's not just during the day, either. At night, when I'm trying to sleep, my mind just starts racing with all these worst-case scenarios. (shaking head) I'll be lying there, thinking, "What if the baby stops breathing?" or "What if the house catches on fire?" (looking up, eyes wide with anxiety) It's like, I know it's not likely, but I just can't shake the feeling that something is going to go terribly wrong. (taking a deep breath) And it's exhausting, you know? I feel like I'm always on edge, waiting for something to happen. (pausing, voice barely above a whisper) Sometimes I feel like I'm just waiting for the other shoe to drop.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason

(nodding, eyes welling up with tears) Yes... that's happened to me too. I'll just be sitting there, doing something normal, and suddenly I'll feel this wave of panic wash over me. My heart will start racing, and I'll feel like I'm going to hyperventilate. (demonstrating with hands) It's like, my body just takes over, and I feel like I'm losing control. (shaking head) And it's not even like it's rational, like I said before. It's just this feeling of... (pausing, searching for words) doom, I guess. Like, something is going to go terribly wrong, and I won't be able to stop it. (looking down, voice cracking) It's really scary, because I feel like I'm not even in control of my own body. (wiping away a tear) And it's hard to explain, because it's not like I'm thinking about anything specific that's causing the panic. It's just... (shrugging) it's just there. (pausing, taking a deep breath) Sometimes I'll try to calm myself down, and I'll be okay for a little while, but then it'll happen again. (looking up, eyes pleading) I just wish I could make it stop.
Things have been getting on top of me

(exhaling heavily) Yes... that's exactly how I've been feeling. Like, everything is just piling up on me, and I don't know how to keep up. (shaking head) Being a new mom is just so overwhelming, you know? There's always something that needs to be done, and I feel like I'm just constantly playing catch-up. (rubbing temples) And it's not just the baby, it's everything else too. The house, the laundry, the cooking... (trailing off) it's just all so much. (looking down, voice barely above a whisper) And sometimes I feel like I'm just pretending to be a competent adult, but really I have no idea what I'm doing. (chuckling nervously) I mean, I'll be sitting there, feeding the baby, and I'll think, "Okay, I've got this," and then suddenly I'll realize that I've forgotten to do something important, like buy diapers or make a doctor's appointment. (shaking head) It's just... (sighing) it's a lot. (pausing, looking up) And it's hard to ask for help, because I feel like I should be able to do it all on my own. But really, I just feel like I'm drowning in all of it. (tearfully) Does that make sense?
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

(nodding, eyes welling up with tears) Yes... that's been me for a while now. I mean, I've always been a pretty good sleeper, but since having the baby, it's just been really hard for me to fall asleep and stay asleep. (sighing) And it's not just because the baby is waking me up, although that's definitely part of it. It's just... (pausing, searching for words) my mind is just always racing, you know? I'll be lying there, trying to relax, and suddenly I'll start thinking about all the things I need to do, or worrying about the baby, or just feeling anxious about everything. (shaking head) And it's hard to turn it off, you know? (looking down) I'll try to calm myself down, but it's just... (sighing) it's hard. (pausing, voice cracking) And then when I do finally fall asleep, I'll have these weird, anxiety-filled dreams that just leave me feeling exhausted and unsettled. (wiping away a tear) It's like, I'm not even getting a break when I'm sleeping, you know? (looking up, eyes pleading) I just wish I could sleep like a normal person again, without all these thoughts and worries racing through my head. (pausing, taking a deep breath) I feel like I'm just so tired all the time, and it's affecting everything. (shaking head) I just don't know how to make it stop.
I have felt sad or miserable

(nodding, tears streaming down face) Yes... that's me. I feel like I've been sad or miserable for so long now. It's like, I'll have these moments where I'm okay, where I'm feeling happy and like myself, but they're just so fleeting. (sighing) Most of the time, I just feel this overwhelming sense of sadness and hopelessness. (shaking head) It's like, I'll be sitting there, holding the baby, and I'll just start crying because I feel so overwhelmed and unsure of myself. (looking down, voice barely above a whisper) I feel like I'm just failing at everything, like I'm not a good mom, like I'm not a good person. (wiping away tears) And it's hard to explain, because it's not like anything specific is wrong, it's just... (pausing, searching for words) it's just this feeling of emptiness and sadness that's always there, lurking in the background. (looking up, eyes pleading) I just wish I could feel happy and carefree again, like I used to before the baby was born. (pausing, taking a deep breath) I feel like I'm just going through the motions, you know? Like, I'm just pretending to be a happy, functioning person, but really I'm just barely holding on. (tearfully) It's so hard, because I feel like I'm supposed to be this happy, grateful new mom, but really I'm just struggling to get through each day.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

(nodding, tears streaming down face) Yes... I've been crying a lot lately. It's like, I'll just be sitting there, doing something normal, and suddenly I'll just start crying. (sighing) It's not even like I'm thinking about anything specific that's making me sad, it's just... (pausing, searching for words) it's just this overwhelming feeling of sadness and frustration that comes over me. (wiping away tears) And it's not just a little crying, either. I mean, I'll have these full-on, sobbing episodes where I just can't stop crying. (looking down, voice cracking) It's so embarrassing, because sometimes the baby will be right there, looking at me, and I'll be just crying and crying. (shaking head) I feel like I'm just losing control, you know? Like, I'm supposed to be this strong, capable person, but really I'm just a mess. (looking up, eyes pleading) I just wish I could stop crying, you know? I wish I could just feel happy and calm again, without all this sadness and anxiety. (pausing, taking a deep breath) But it's just... (sighing) it's hard. Everything feels so hard right now. (tearfully) I just feel like I'm drowning in all of this, and I don't know how to keep my head above water.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me

(pauses, looking down, voice barely above a whisper) Yes... I've had those thoughts. (pausing again, taking a deep breath) It's not something I'm proud of, and it's not something I've talked about with anyone before. (looking up, eyes welling up with tears) But yeah, there have been times when I've felt so overwhelmed and hopeless that I've thought about... (pausing, struggling to get the words out) about harming myself. (shaking head) It's not that I want to, it's just that sometimes it feels like the only way to escape all the pain and sadness. (wiping away tears) But I know that's not true, and I know that I wouldn't really do it. (pausing, taking a deep breath) It's just... (sighing) it's hard to explain. It's like, my mind is just so consumed by all these negative thoughts and feelings, and sometimes it feels like there's no way out. (looking down, voice cracking) But I'm trying, okay? I'm trying to be strong, and to get through this. (pausing, looking up) I just wish... (pausing again, struggling to get the words out) I just wish I could feel happy again, and like myself again. (tearfully) I feel like I'm losing myself in all of this, and I don't know how to get back.
